chapter: Eddie Heywood, the organ and later work
title: T-Bone Walker, Norman Granz and San Diego concerts
summary: He knew T-Bone from the Plantation, when Norman Granz arranged concerts and sessions at Billy Berg's before JATP.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: Now, coming a little closer, you went to Europe in '68 with T-Bone Walker.
Now, how was that? You hadn't accompanied Blues singers much before.

Well, I played with T-Bone back in the days when...at the Plantation, when John Kirby was there. And also there was a fellow there working in a real estate office. His name was Norman Granz. And he got us to play concerts down at the high school in San Diego. And T-Bone and I used to ride down there, with Oscar Pettiford, Sir Charles Thompson, Red Nichols and his Pennies and Nat Cole...
You mean this is before Jazz at the Philharmonic.

Yeah, he was doing sessions at Billy Berg's. The intermission piano player was Andre Previn. And (?) played was Coleman Hawkins, Sir Charles on piano, Denzil Best... And I did not show up... They booked me at the Philharmonic, but Calvin Jackson took my place; I was sick or something. So T-Bone Walker and I knew each other from back in Los Angeles.
